text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose 0.31% today to close at $388.90, capping a strong week-long rally of 7.81% since late August. The gains reflect a tightening global refining market: diesel prices hit record highs this week as Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries knock those facilities offline and Russia bans diesel exports, while U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity utilization. For a major U.S. refiner, this supply crunch translates directly into wider profit margins on fuel production—the refiner earns more per barrel of crude oil it processes when refined products become scarcer and more valuable.

The broader geopolitical backdrop amplifies the tailwind. This week brought news of escalating sanctions on Iran (from the EU joining a U.S.-led campaign) and military efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, along with Trump's new Venezuela oil deal—all moves that could reshape global crude supplies in ways that favor domestic U.S. refiners. Against this backdrop of tighter global refining capacity and higher fuel prices, Marathon's stock momentum reflects investor confidence that refining margins will remain elevated in the near term.
